<noinclude><pagequality level="3" user="Mathmitch7" />{{rh|Ioſeph talketh|Geneſis|with his brethren.}} {{rule}} <!-- useful info for KJV Common characters: ſ ¶ ⁊ ⸗ <sup>†</sup>{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text-align=left|text=† ''Note text''}} *{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text-align=left|text=* Note text}} ‖{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text-align=left|text=‖ ''Note text''}}  Remember that v and u are combined, "v" appears at beginnings of words and "u" in the middle Remember that i and j are combined, use "i" or "I" in all cases.--></noinclude>twelve brethren, the ſonnes of one man in the land of Canaan: and, behold, the youngeſt {{smaller|is}} this day with our father, and one is not.

{{verse|42|14}}And Ioſeph ſaid vnto them, That {{smaller|is}} {{smaller|it}} that I ſpake vnto you, ſaying, Ye {{smaller|are}} ſpies.

{{verse|42|15}}Hereby ye ſhall be proued: by the life of Pharaoh ye ſhall not goe foorth hence, except your youngeſt brother come hither.

{{verse|42|16}}Send one of you, and let him fetch your brother, and ye ſhalbe <sup>†</sup>{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text-align=left|text=† ''Heb. bound''}} kept in priſon, that your wordes may be proued, whether {{smaller|there}} {{smaller|be}} {{smaller|any}} trueth in you: or els by the life of Pharaoh ſurely ye {{smaller|are}} ſpies.

{{verse|42|17}}And he <sup>†</sup>{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text-align=left|text=† ''Hebr. gathered.''}} put them all together into warde, three dayes.

{{verse|42|18}}And Ioſeph ſaid vnto them the third day, This doe, and liue: {{smaller|for}} I feare God.

{{verse|42|19}}If ye {{smaller|be}} true {{smaller|men}}, let one of your brethren be bound in the houſe of your priſon: goe ye, carry corne for the famine of your houſes.

{{verse|42|20}}But *{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text-align=left|text=* Chap.43.5.}} bring your yongeſt brother vnto mee, ſo ſhall your wordes be verified, and yee ſhall not die: and they did ſo.

{{verse|42|21}}¶ And they ſaid one to another, We {{smaller|are}} verily guiltie concerning our brother, in that we ſaw the anguiſh of his ſoule, when he beſought vs, and we would not heare: therefore is this diſtreſſe come vpon vs.

{{verse|42|22}}And Reuben anſwered them, ſaying, *{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text-align=left|text=* Chap.37.21.}} Spake I not vnto you, ſaying, Doe not ſinne againſt the childe, and ye would not heare? therefore behold alſo, his blood is required.

{{verse|42|23}}And they knew not that Ioſeph vnderſtood {{smaller|them}}: for <sup>†</sup>{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text-align=left|text=† ''Hebr. an interpreter was betweene them.''}} hee ſpake vnto them by an interpreter.

{{verse|42|24}}And hee turned himſelfe about from them and wept, and returned to them againe, and communed with them, and tooke from them Simeon, and bound him before their eyes.

{{verse|42|25}}¶ Then Ioſeph commanded to fill their ſackes with corne, and to reſtore euery mans money into his ſacke, and to giue them prouiſion for the way: and thus did he vnto them.

{{verse|42|26}}And they laded their aſſes with the corne, and departed thence.

{{verse|42|27}}And as one of them opened his ſacke, to giue his aſſe prouender in the Inne, he eſpied his money: for behold, it {{smaller|was}} in his ſackes mouth.

{{verse|42|28}}And he ſaid vnto his brethren, My money is reſtored, and loe, {{smaller|it is}} euen in my ſacke: and their heart <sup>†</sup>{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text-align=left|text=† ''Hebr. went foorth.''}} failed them, and they were afraid, ſaying one to an other, What is this that God hath done to vs?

{{verse|42|29}}¶ And they came vnto Iacob their father, vnto the land of Canaan, and told him all that befell vnto them, ſaying;

{{verse|42|30}}The man {{smaller|who is}} the lord of the land, ſpake <sup>†</sup>{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text-align=left|text=† ''Hebr. with vs hard things.''}} roughly with vs, and tooke vs for ſpies of the countrey.

{{verse|42|31}}And we ſaid vnto him, We {{smaller|are}} true {{smaller|men}}; we are no ſpies.

{{verse|42|32}}We {{smaller|be}} twelue brethren, ſonnes of our father: one {{smaller|is}} not, and the yongeſt {{smaller|is}} this day with our father, in the land of Canaan.

{{verse|42|33}}And the man the lord of the countrey ſaid vnto vs, Hereby ſhall I know that ye are true men: leaue one of your brethren here with me, and take {{smaller|foode}} for the famine of your houſholds, and be gone.

{{verse|42|34}}And bring your yongeſt brother vnto me: then ſhall I know that you {{smaller|are}} no ſpies, but {{smaller|that}} you {{smaller|are}} true men: {{smaller|ſo}} will I deliuer your brother, and ye ſhall traffique in the land.

{{verse|42|35}}¶ And it came to paſſe as they emptied their ſacks, that behold, euery mans bundle of money {{smaller|was}} in his ſacke: and when {{smaller|both}} they and their father ſaw the bundels of money, they were afraid.

{{verse|42|36}}And Iacob their father ſaid vnto them, We haue ye bereaued of my children: Ioſeph is not, and Simeon is not, and ye wil take Beniamin {{smaller|away}}: all theſe things are againſt me.

{{verse|42|37}}And Reuben ſpake vnto his father, ſaying; Slay my two ſonnes, if I bring him not to thee: deliuer him into my hand, and I will bring him to thee againe.

{{verse|42|38}}And he ſaid, My ſonne ſhall not goe downe with you, for his brother is dead, and he is left alone: if miſchiefe befall him by the way in the which yee goe, then ſhall ye bring downe my gray haires with ſorrow to the graue.

==={{Chapter|43|CHAP. XLIII.}}===

{{smaller block|[[#43:1|1]] Iacob is hardly perſwaded to ſend Beniamin.. [[#43:15|15]] Ioſeph entertaineth his brethren. [[#43:31|31]] Hee maketh them a feaſt.}}
